doc.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012

title: Early band experience, the butterfly-bomb death of a drummer, and VE Day
summary: He had learned from a drummer in an Artie Shaw type band; a cinema drummer was killed by a butterfly bomb. He remembers dancing in the street on VE Day.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Did you have band experience before you went with them?

Yes. I studied with a drummer who used to let me sit next to him when he was playing with an Artie Shaw type big band. So this was great, great, a great opportunity for me. And occasionally he would take off himself. Eventually he retired I think, and I got the job. Prior to that I was working in a cinema with a little band, prior to the movies, and the drummer, starting home one night, saw one of these butterfly bombs. He walked up to it and it killed him.
I was going to ask about that, if you knew anybody that had encountered them.

One night they dropped three thousand of these things on our town. And incendiary bombs as well. And that was basically the bulk of the bombing. I guess as we started to move into Germany and, with the second world war, the invasion.
What do you remember about VE day?

I remember dancing on the street. Yeah. Everyone was kissing everybody and we were all dancing. And oh it was crazy. I remember the day that they invaded too, with the invasion. I was on the dock still, of working as apprentice compass adjuster. That was ’45.
